text:
alex: Quick Q — PR <https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood/pull/4221|#4221> adds /v3/classify. We changed error shapes a bit and I want to lock down semantics before we merge. Specifically: which HTTP codes should mean 'do not retry' vs 'safe to retry'? Our mobile SDK currently retries on 5xx and 429, but treats 400 as non-retryable. Should validation failures be 400 or 422?

maria: my vote: 400 = bad/malformed request (e.g. invalid JSON, incorrect content-type), 422 = semantic validation (input schema, prompt length etc) and should be non-retryable. Keep 429 for rate limit (retryable with backoff). 5xx = server/transient (retryable). :+1:

sanjay: Agree with maria. Also: important for backward compatibility — older clients expect an "error.message" string and sometimes parse a top-level "message". The integration tests flagged that we removed the top-level message. We should keep both for a release cycle. Minimal shape suggestion (keeps old field and new structured error):

```
{
  "error": {
    "type": "validation_error",
    "message": "input too long",
    "retryable": false,
    "code": 422
  },
  "message": "input too long"
}
```

This makes it explicit for SDKs and doesn't break naive parsers.

devbot: Integration test: error-shape-backcompat failed on staging (see logs). Failing clients: iOS SDK v1.4.2 and python-sdk v0.9.7.

alex: OK — so plan: 1) return 422 for semantic validation + include both nested "error.message" and top-level "message"; 2) 400 reserved for parse/malformed requests; 3) 429 for rate-limit; 4) 5xx retryable; 5) streaming: if midstream validation hits, emit an error event with same shape and then close the stream (clients should treat it as non-retryable unless they can resume). Thoughts?

maria: streaming detail: yes — emit an error frame, include same error object and a final control frame. Document it. Also add a short migration note in changelog and mark as a non-breaking additive change.

sanjay: SDK impacts: I'll add handling so SDKs treat 422 as non-retryable. One caveat: idempotency/duplicate-detection — if an idempotency conflict occurs we might return 409; SDKs should surface that to caller (not auto-retry).

alex: For rollout, I'm going to gate this behind a feature flag and canary to 5% traffic. @eng-oncall — please watch for 5xx spike during canary.

eng-oncall: Roger. I'll set up an alert for error-rate > 0.5% and token-latency regressions. Ping me if you want a temporary uplift on retention for traces.

maria: Small request: add an e2e test that asserts both the top-level "message" exists and the nested error.type is present. Also add a test asserting SDKs do not retry on 422.

alex: Will do. @sanjay can you review #4221 when I push the tests? leaving a small change to add back top-level message. :eyes:

sanjay: I'll take a look today. If it's small, we can merge post-canary. :thumbsup:

alex: Thanks — merging plan: feature-flag + canary + docs + tests. I'll update the PR description with the error shape and SDK guidance. Closing this thread after PR update.
